item.title: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02808-5

The contribution of glacial lakes to glacier mass loss is unclear. This work maps global glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020 to quantify changes in number, volume and area, showing that they explain 11 ± 7% of lake-terminating glacier loss, with climate forcing and glacier geometry the dominant factors.

item.title: Concurrent atmospheric phenomena amplify precipitation extremes under anthropogenic climate change
item.content:encoded:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02805-8

Extreme precipitation events are increasing in many regions. Here the authors discuss how the increasing concurrence of atmospheric phenomena could contribute to these trends under anthropogenic warming.
